subject: Liability cap: annual-reset vs cumulative — proposed language and next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Liability cap: annual-reset vs cumulative — need quick take

Team —

Attaching the customer redlines (MSA_redline_v3.docx) and our current Order Form. Nimbus is pushing back on our liability cap language; their initial position is that the cap should be a single cumulative cap tied to fees paid under the Agreement (they don't want an annual reset). They also trimmed several carveouts and tightened IP/indemnity language.

Key asks:
- Legal: preferred position on annual-reset (reset every 12 months) vs cumulative total (aggregate across term) and a suggested concrete clause we can present to them.
- Procurement/finance: run the 12-month and cumulative scenarios for the forecasted first-year spend (I pasted the numbers in redline-summary.xlsx).
- Ops: any operational risk to an annual-reset approach we should call out (billing complexities, reporting).

Customer points to CFO concerns about open-ended exposure. Our negotiating goals are: keep an operationally simple calculation, preserve carveouts for IP breach/data breach/gross negligence, and keep exposure bounded (either a multiple of fees or a fixed floor).

Proposed starting language (from draft):
"Liability Cap: Except for liability arising from (a) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (b) infringement of third-party intellectual property rights, and (c) breaches of confidentiality and data protection obligations, each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood Inference under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim or (ii) USD 500,000. The cap shall reset on each anniversary of the Effective Date.
"
I want short, actionable feedback by EOD Pacific so we can circle back with Maria (Nimbus) tomorrow and attach a one-page rationale for finance.

Thanks —

On Fri, Nov 6, 2026 at 3:04 PM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> (see above)

Quick legal take:
1) Practical default — annual-reset tied to 12 months of fees is clean and measurable. For customers with variable consumption it limits each year’s exposure and aligns with how order forms are invoiced.
2) Backstop floor — recommend including a fixed-floor safety net (e.g., the greater of 12 months fees or USD 750,000). That prevents extremely low caps in year 1 for small pilots.
3) Carveouts — accept carveouts for (i) willful misconduct/gross negligence, (ii) IP infringement indemnity, (iii) breaches of confidentiality/data protection, and (iv) death/personal injury. Do not extend carveouts to service credits or performance SLAs — those remain subject to the cap.
4) Data breach approach — customer will push for uncapped liability here. Counter with a limited indemnity tied to direct costs (notice, credit monitoring) and require proof/limits; also tie to cyber insurance minimums rather than open-ended exposure.

Suggested redline language for MSA (short):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of either party for all claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Provider under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (ii) USD 750,000; provided, however, that liability for (A) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (B) infringement of a third party's intellectual property rights, and (C) breaches of confidentiality or data protection obligations shall not be limited by this Section."

I'll flag the insurance/damage items in a short memo we can attach. If procurement wants sample math language for the Order Form, say so and I'll draft.

- Marcus

Subject: Re: Liability cap: annual-reset vs cumulative — need quick take

Agree with Marcus. A couple of practical notes from procurement:
- For customers that ramp quickly, an annual-reset works in our favor (it prevents a long tail cumulative exposure from early pilot years).
- Finance will want explicit calculation language in the Order Form: "Liability cap calculation = sum of all amounts invoiced to Customer under the Order Form during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date the claim is first made." Put an example: if invoices in months 1-12 total $420k, the cap for a claim on month 14 is $420k (subject to the fixed floor).
- If we go to a floor of USD 750k, ask finance to run a sensitivity: what's the % of deals that fall below that in year 1? I hooked redline-summary.xlsx with a simple model.

Also recommend we prepare a one-page note for Nimbus' CFO explaining the commercial rationale for the annual-reset + floor approach versus cumulative. If they insist on cumulative, we should get them to agree to either (i) a higher floor or (ii) carveouts for a data-breach indemnity with insured limits.

Karthik

Subject: Re: Liability cap: annual-reset vs cumulative — need quick take

Stephanie —

Thank you for the quick turn. Nimbus' position from Finance is that a cumulative cap tied to fees paid under the Agreement (aggregate across the Term) is the only acceptable construct for them — annual resets artificially limit exposure for mature customers and do not match our CFO's risk model.

Our team is prepared to narrow the carveouts to the following: (1) willful misconduct; (2) infringement of third-party intellectual property rights. We will not accept a carveout for general data breach liability; instead our insurance team prefers a clear cyber policy requirement and a specified cap on direct remediation costs.

I have attached Nimbus' proposed redlines for the MSA (Nimbus_redlines.docx). We are willing to discuss a middle ground on the floor number but cannot accept language that results in a cap higher than total fees paid under the Order Form. To move this forward, can you provide: (a) a short commercial rationale we can share with our CFO for why Redwood prefers annual reset, (b) a worked example comparing cumulative vs annual reset for the first 24 months of typical deployment, and (c) your proposed wording for cyber/data breach indemnity (amounts and linkage to insurance)?

If helpful, Elliot from our external counsel is looped in to accelerate legal language. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call Monday if that helps.

Regards,

Thanks Maria — appreciate the clarity.

Plan / proposed compromise for discussion with Nimbus on Monday:
1) Offer two options formally in the MSA and Order Form appendix so Finance can pick:
   A) Annual-reset option: Cap = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) USD 750,000; cap resets each anniversary.
   B) Cumulative option: Cap = aggregate fees paid under the Agreement (cumulative); if Nimbus selects this, Redwood requests a higher floor (suggest USD 1,250,000) and explicit cyber indemnity carveouts limited to direct remediation costs (with sub-cap tied to insurance).
2) Carveouts — agree to narrow list per negotiations, but retain IP and willful misconduct carveouts as non-limited. For data breaches we propose an indemnity limited to direct remediation (notice, credit monitoring) up to USD X and require minimum cyber insurance (we will propose language).
3) Deliverables Monday: one-page rationale for CFO (annual-reset commercial logic), a 2-column worked example for months 1–24, and Marcus will draft the two MSA options plus cyber indemnity language. Karthik/Finance will provide the sensitivity numbers.

If that approach looks OK to legal and procurement internally, I'll send Maria a short note outlining the two options and propose a call Monday at 10am PT to resolve final language.
